description: Marks one stage of one run as started, creating its run_stages row on first attempt or re-opening it on a resume/re-run (ADR-014). Committed immediately so a concurrent reader (the UI) observes the transition without waiting for the stage itself to finish.
signature: def begin_run_stage(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, stage: str) -> int
docstring:
Transition one run_stages row to 'running', creating it if absent.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run this stage belongs to. Must already exist in runs.
    stage: One of 'acquisition', 'enrichment', 'analysis'.

Returns:
    The new attempt number (1 for a first attempt, incremented on every subsequent call for the same run_id/stage).

Raises:
    StorageError: If run_id does not exist, or stage is not one of the three allowed values.
postconditions: read_run_stages(conn, run_id) includes a row for stage with status='running', started_at set, finished_at and error_message cleared to NULL
The returned attempt number equals the row's attempt column after the call
The write is committed before begin_run_stage returns (ADR-016: the pipeline's own subsequent data writes for this stage must be able to assume this status is already visible to a reader)

edge_cases.input: First attempt of a stage for a given run_id (no existing row)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: row is created with attempt=1, status='running'

edge_cases.input: Stage was previously 'succeeded' and begin_run_stage is called again (resume or deliberate re-run after a parameter change)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: legal; attempt increments, status resets to 'running', finished_at and error_message are cleared -- this is how ADR-014 resume and ADR-009 stage re-runs both work

edge_cases.input: Stage is currently 'running' (e.g. a stale row from a crashed process, see reconcile_orphaned_runs in orchestration)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: storage does not itself detect staleness; it re-opens the row as instructed. Detecting and reconciling an orphaned 'running' row on startup is orchestration's responsibility, not storage's

edge_cases.input: stage='orchestration' or any value outside the CHECK-constrained set

unit_tests.name: test_first_attempt_creates_row
unit_tests.description: Calling begin_run_stage for a stage never attempted creates the row with attempt=1.
unit_tests.expected: returns 1; read_run_stages shows one row, status='running'

unit_tests.name: test_reattempt_increments_and_resets
unit_tests.description: A second begin_run_stage call for the same run_id/stage after finish_run_stage('succeeded') increments attempt and clears finished_at/error_message.

unit_tests.name: test_unknown_run_id_raises
unit_tests.description: begin_run_stage for a run_id absent from runs raises StorageError.

unit_tests.name: test_invalid_stage_raises
unit_tests.description: An out-of-vocabulary stage name raises StorageError before any write.
